articles.title: In 2013, Addison Lee founder John Griffin paid £20.7 million for a Regent’s Park mansion and later asked £32 million; 13 years later, the six-bedroom home has sold for £11.5 million
articles.summary: John Griffin, the founder of London taxi company Addison Lee, experienced what can only be described as a bad day after selling his London mansion
articles.body: John Griffin, the founder of London taxi company Addison Lee, experienced what can only be described as a bad day after selling his London mansion overlooking Regent’s Park, leaving him with a loss of about £9.2 million, according to a report by The Telegraph. He bought the six-bedroom house on Hanover Terrace in 2013 for £20.7 million. Thirteen years later, the mansion was sold for £11.5 million. For a man who once sold his taxi firm for a fortune, this property gamble wasn’t quite worth it.Sold for nearly half the price he paid 13 years agoThe mansion sits on Hanover Terrace, in the heart of Regent’s Park. Part of a Regency-era row, the six-bedroom mansion was designed by the architect John Nash. The mansion was sold at the beginning of October for a 44% discount, according to a Bloomberg report.Griffin bought the house in the same year he sold his taxi firm, Addison Lee, to the Carlyle Group for about £300 million. He paid £20.7 million for the mansion in 2013, filings show.The house was first put on the market at a much higher price. Multiple reports suggested the mansion was listed in 2021 for £32 million. Even after several price cuts, it didn’t find a buyer. The property was taken off the market before returning this year at £13.5 million. The final sale price came in below that figure, reports say.The sale comes a month after he lost a drawn-out battle with UK tax authorities.For years, Griffin has been fighting HMRC, the UK tax authority, over his tax residency. He argued that he should qualify for non-domiciled status between 2013 and 2020. That status would have kept income earned abroad outside the scope of UK tax. But in September, a tribunal ruled against him. The sale was agreed before that ruling and completed less than a month after it, according to a person familiar with the process. It is unclear whether the verdict affected the final price.Griffin’s sale fits a wider pattern. London’s prime property market has suffered in recent months amid tax changes and economic and political uncertainty. Estate agent JLL’s residential research data shows that 457 homes worth more than £5 million were sold in central London between July and September, The National News reported. That was 11% fewer than in the previous quarter. Many of the city’s priciest properties have been hit by these tax changes and economic and political shocks.Property analysts LonRes told the publication that the prime London market saw a slowdown this summer, with average sale prices 7.9% lower in July than a year earlier and 5.7% lower than during the pre-Covid period. A property in Notting Hill sold for £25.9 million during the same period, even as prices fell around it.“Adding a new prime minister and continuing global uncertainty to the mix has resulted in a subdued prime London market, with the super-prime segment particularly affected. The key indicator is simply the number of transactions relative to new instructions, under offers and existing stock – it remains stubbornly low. Uncertainty and a lack of urgency, driven in part by low expectations of future price growth, continue to hinder any potential recovery,” LonRes told the outlet.“At the top end of the market, fewer people need to buy or sell, so the issues are amplified. Last year, we saw a prolonged slowdown as pre-budget tax speculation started in the summer and carried on all the way to the end of the year,” it added.In some areas, the slowdown has had little effect. Earlier this year, The Holme in Regent’s Park sold for a profit of about £56 million. The house had been taken out of receivership less than two years earlier for £139 million.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.summary: HYDERABAD: Food regulator FSSAI has issued notices to Hyderabad-based Gemini Edibles & Fats India Ltd, BigBasket and Flipkart for allegedly making
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Food regulator FSSAI has issued notices to Hyderabad-based Gemini Edibles & Fats India Ltd, BigBasket and Flipkart for allegedly making misleading health claims while selling rice bran oil.In a social media post on Friday, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said notices had been issued to Gemini Edibles & Fats India, Innovative Retail Concepts (BigBasket) and Flipkart India over claims related to the product ‘Freedom Cooking Rice Bran Oil’.The product was promoted through e-commerce platforms and social media with claims such as “Reduces bad cholesterol and maintains/increases good cholesterol” and “10,000+ PPM Natural Oryzanol”, the regulator said, news agency PTI reported.“The cholesterol and heart-health claims were found to be not covered/permitted under the applicable claims for edible vegetable oil (rice bran oil) under the Advertising and Claims Regulations, 2018,” FSSAI said.The regulator also found that Gemini Edibles & Fats India was offering and selling food products through its own e-commerce website without appearing to hold a valid central licence covering e-commerce activity.The three food business operators have been directed to show cause why action should not be initiated against them under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, PTI reported.Separately, FSSAI has suspended the licence of DNV Food Products Ltd following an inspection that revealed serious non-compliances related to hygiene, sanitation, storage and licensing.The regulator has also cancelled the licence of Jhanvittanni for continued non-compliance with food safety rules and regulations.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Bait bomb made in neighbouring Deogarh with goat skin
articles.summary: Odisha forest officials say a bait bomb made with decomposed goat skin, sourced from Deogarh, killed a wild boar in Angul; four arrested, more seized.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: Forest officials on Friday revealed that dried and decomposed goat skin was used to make the bait bomb that killed a wild boar in Biripal reserve forest under Angul forest division on Tuesday night.The strong smell of the goat skin reportedly attracted the animal, which bit into the explosive-laced bait, triggering a fatal blast.According to officials, the crude bombs were not manufactured in Angul district but were brought from neighbouring Deogarh. The forest department has sought police assistance to trace the source of the explosives and identify those involved in their production. “We are trying to ascertain who are making these bombs and where they are being manufactured. In this case, interrogation of the four accused revealed that the bombs were prepared in Deogarh district,” Kaniha range officer Debadatta Sutar said.The wildlife wing of the forest department arrested four persons during a night patrol operation conducted by the Rengali forester and his team in Gandamala beat under the Rengali section of Kaniha range. Besides recovering the carcass of a male wild boar killed by the explosion, officials seized six live bait bombs concealed inside edible material.Forest authorities said the timely seizure prevented further wildlife casualties. Bait bombs are considered among the cruellest methods of hunting as they are designed to explode when bitten by animals, causing devastating injuries and often death.Wildlife officials warned that such devices pose a threat not only to wild animals but also to livestock and humans who may accidentally come into contact with them.The incident has revived concerns over the growing use of bait bombs in Odisha. Two months ago, a bull on the fringes of Chandaka wildlife sanctuary near Banki accidentally consumed a bait bomb allegedly meant for a wild boar. The explosion caused severe injuries inside its mouth and despite prolonged veterinary treatment, the animal later died.Forest officials said efforts are underway to dismantle the network behind the manufacture and supply of the deadly traps.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhubaneswar | Silver Rate in Bhubaneswar | Bank Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Public Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Petrol Price in Bhubaneswar | Diesel Price in Bhubaneswar | CNG Price in Bhubaneswar | LPG Price in BhubaneswarStay updated with the latest Bhubaneswar news. articles.title: Hunger strike over BSL jobs for displaced families enters 7th day
articles.summary: Bokaro Steel Plant job hunger strike by displaced families enters day 7, blocking multiple gates; several hospitalized as talks sought over apprentices and hiring policy.
articles.body: Bokaro: An indefinite hunger strike by hundreds of displaced persons demanding jobs at the Bokaro Steel Plant (BSL) entered its seventh day on Friday, with the protest intensifying into a blockade of several plant gates.More than a dozen protesters, including women, were admitted to hospital in the last 24 hours after their health deteriorated during the fast, which began at Two Tank Garden near the BSL headquarters on Oct 10, protesters said.The agitators had closed Steel Gate No. 9 and Dugal Gate No. 10 on Thursday. On Friday, after what they described as a lack of positive response from BSL management, they blocked gates 3, 4 and 5, besides the CZ Gate and Mansa Singh Gate. The protesters threatened to shut the main gate on Saturday.Bokaro Congress MLA Shwettaa Singh, who has joined the agitators, said the protest was peaceful but warned that the blockade could affect plant operations. “We are ready for talks, but no senior decision-maker from BSL has come to us in seven days,” she said.The protesters, under the banner of Visthapit Apprentice Sangh, are demanding reinstatement of displaced apprentice trainees, restoration of the earlier reservation system for Class IV jobs, regular appointments and a clear employment policy for families displaced by the steel plant. They said families who gave up land for the plant should get priority in jobs and should not be pushed into contractual work.The blockade affected employee movement and triggered concern over operations. A contract worker at the sinter plant said workers who usually enter through Gate No. 3 were forced to use the Main Gate; he said he abandoned his trip because of the disruption.The agitation has received support from BJP, Congress and JKLM. Dumri MLA and JKLM chief Jairam Mahto visited the protest site, while Dhanbad BJP MP Dulu Mahato extended support on Thursday. Senior Congress members, including state ministers, are expected to visit the site on Saturday.Bokaro deputy commissioner Ajay Nath Jha has asked BSL to begin talks. The PSU said 204 of 950 displaced apprentices had been given contractual employment by Oct 3.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Safety advisory for Durga Puja idol immersion in Hazaribag
articles.summary: Hazaribag issues safety guidelines for Durga Puja idol immersion: notify safe sites, restrict unsafe locations, ensure barricading, lighting, lifeguards and rescue gear.
articles.body: Hazaribag: To prevent drowning incidents and ensure devotees’ safety during Durga Puja idol immersion at rivers, ponds, lakes, waterfalls and other water bodies, safety guidelines have been issued by Hazaribag District Disaster Management Authority.Authorities have been directed to identify and notify safe immersion sites based on local conditions, while immersion at unsafe or prohibited locations will be restricted. Officials have also been asked to assess water depth, currents, slippery surfaces and other potential hazards in advance.The guidelines mandate adequate barricading, lighting, warning signs and safe entry and exit arrangements at immersion sites. Wherever feasible, temporary or artificial immersion tanks should be set up to reduce entry into natural water bodies.The authority has also emphasised the deployment of trained lifeguards, divers and water rescue personnel at major immersion points. Essential rescue equipment, including life jackets, lifebuoys, rescue ropes and boats, must be kept ready.Deputy commissioner Hemant Sati urged officials and puja organisers to strictly follow the safety protocols to prevent any mishap during idol immersion.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news.
